settings.headline: The most powerful thing you can do for your child's first words is already in your hands.
settings.body:
Decades of research are clear about this: the time a parent spends talking, playing, and reading with their child is the single biggest factor in early language development. Not flashcards. Not screens. Not waiting until the next pediatrician visit.

You already do this every day. The only thing missing is a simple, joyful tool that turns that time into something even more meaningful.

That's what these books are for.

settings.headline_main: What happens in a speech therapy session?
settings.body:
A pediatric SLP doesn't pull out flashcards or run drills. She reads a book. She makes a silly sound. She pauses. She waits. She celebrates every tiny try — every gesture, every babble, every brave attempt.

That's the whole magic of it. Children learn language through joyful, back-and-forth play with people they love. The only difference between her reading time and yours is that she knows which sounds, which words, and which little pauses help most at each stage.
settings.quote_text: The most powerful thing a parent can do isn't more time — it's a few small techniques used with love. These books are those techniques, written right onto the page. Anyone can use them.

settings.headline: Hi, I'm Stephanie
settings.body:
I'm a pediatric speech-language pathologist, mom, and the founder of Speech Therapy Publishing. After years of working one-on-one with toddlers and their families, I wanted to put the gentle techniques I use every day into something parents could pick up and use too.

That's how these books came to be — written for the parent who wants to make their child's reading time the most powerful part of the day, with no special training required.
settings.credentials: Stephanie Anderson, M.S., CCC-SLP · Pediatric Speech-Language Pathologist · Founder, Twin Cities Speech Therapy Publishing

settings.question: What age are these books for?
settings.answer: The books are made for babies and toddlers from about 6 months through age 4. The Imitation Book is a beautiful starting point as early as 6 months; My Words Book opens up around 12 months; Action Book bridges to early sentences from around 18 months. Most families come back to all three at different stages.

settings.question: What makes these different from other board books?
settings.answer: Most board books focus on illustrations and a story. These are built around the gentle techniques speech therapists already use — imitation, pause-and-wait, joyful repetition, and scaffolded vocabulary — written right into the pages so you have everything you need to spark talking practice as you read.

settings.question: How much time per day does this take?
settings.answer: 10 to 15 minutes a day is plenty. Consistency matters more than length — a short, playful reading most days will do more than one long session a week.

settings.question: Do I really need all three books, or can I start with just one?
settings.answer: You can absolutely start with one. But the books were designed as a system that grows with your child: the Imitation Book builds the foundation, My Words Book adds vocabulary, and Action Book bridges to early sentences. The bundle saves $7.98 and gives you the full arc for the next two to three years.

settings.question: When will I see new words come?
settings.answer: Most parents notice their child engaging more — pointing, gesturing, trying sounds — within the first week or two. New words usually come in 3 to 6 weeks of consistent reading. Every child is different though, and slower bloomers are just as wonderful.

settings.question: What if my child doesn't respond right away?
settings.answer: Totally normal — and totally okay. Some little ones watch quietly for weeks before they try a sound out loud. Keep reading playfully, keep pausing for their turn, and celebrate every little effort — even a glance or a babble counts. The "Pause & Wait" step is the most powerful part.
